hypothesis: Sharing one K/V load across the three query heads of a KV group can reduce repeated texture work. The same fusion is implemented for FP16 to avoid attributing a generic scheduling improvement to ASTC.
primary: T8192: compact GQA ASTC GPU time <=1.05 times BOTH original FP16 and fused GQA FP16 in every one of five sessions, with persistent K/V/metadata bytes <=0.75 of FP16.
positive_criterion: Both timing contrasts pass in all five sessions, memory criterion passes, and all sixteen own-reference attention gates plus original exact decode gates pass.
secondary: Old hoisted ASTC versus shared GQA ASTC; original FP16 versus fused FP16. Neither substitutes for the primary. Existing v8/v9 candidates are retained as correctness controls only.
timing_design: Seeded ABBA or BAAB for four comparisons, random comparison order per block, ten warmup command buffers per variant, retain every sample. Five separately launched sessions, shapes shuffled per session.
scope: Precompressed warm fixtures, D64/Hq9/Hkv3 and one model capture. GQA fusion is known prior art. Each query head retains separate exact softmax states; K/V/affine data are loaded once then reused in registers. Increased live state can erase benefit; no register/occupancy counter claim. No model PPL, full decode, dynamic encoder or production peak result. T2048/T8192 repeat fixture blocks.
